_about: Source of truth for resume.arcs.care/proof and /proof/claims.json. Rendered by scripts/proof_emit.py; never edit public/proof.html or public/proof-claims.json by hand. Every claim carries a status: shown (a public record anyone can open), on-request (a real record that is private: employer data or the private repo; references available), not-yet (no record yet). A claim with status shown must carry a url. Falsification entries are read by id from _STATE/falsification-ledger.jsonl.
subject: Zach Harris

statuses.shown: A public record anyone can open.
statuses.on-request: A real record that is private (employer data or a private repository). References available.
statuses.not-yet: No record yet. Listed so the gap is visible.

questions.answer: Yes. Solo, in production, with a dated record of the work.

claims.evidence: The live app, and a status page that measures the build from the repository itself.
claims.label: status.arcs.care

questions.answer: Yes. SEC, FINRA, HIPAA and GDPR environments, with outcomes to match.

claims.evidence: Client engagement, 2019 to 2020. References available.

claims.claim: Guardrails as code: per-tenant database roles that fail closed, and pre-commit gates that block whole classes of bugs.
claims.evidence: In the private repository; walkthrough on request.

claims.evidence: A migration shipped in code but never reached production, breaking every saved decision for six weeks.

questions.answer: Yes, and he keeps the record: every belief that broke, the test that broke it, and what replaced it.

claims.claim: 42 beliefs logged as overturned, each with the test that overturned it.
claims.evidence: A public falsification ledger. Three of the entries:
claims.label: status.arcs.care/beliefs

ledger_entries.claim: A green Next.js production build means the database layer works.
ledger_entries.test: first real prisma.$queryRaw against prod (a 401 gate meant zero traffic had ever hit the routes).
ledger_entries.delta: green build proves nothing — `prisma generate` never connects, so every create() threw at runtime, unlogged.

ledger_entries.claim: `gh pr checks --watch && gh pr merge` is a sufficient merge gate.
ledger_entries.test: a background watcher merged PR #130 while claude-security-review was RED.
ledger_entries.delta: --watch exits 0 on completion, not on passing — a red X can still merge.

ledger_entries.claim: Content probes (grep/curl) are sufficient to claim a UI is polished and verified.
ledger_entries.test: repeated 'polish' commits verified only by grep; the rail was visibly broken (orphaned dot, 3-line wrap) the whole time.
ledger_entries.delta: text checks prove presence, not layout — a screenshot caught what grep couldn't.

claims.claim: Books his own errors: 14 false receipts the system caught against itself in one week.
claims.evidence: A system that only counts what it built is keeping half a book.
claims.label: Assets and Liabilities

claims.claim: Makes dated public predictions and checks them against what happened.
claims.evidence: Three dated calls about Apple, scored against the outcome.
claims.label: Closing the Loop

claims.claim: Takes hard feedback from strangers: a recruiter called his resume AI slop, and he agreed.
claims.evidence: Notes on the review nobody on your own team can give you.
claims.label: Any Stranger Can Be a Bar Raiser

claims.claim: When an agent sent two emails nobody asked for, he published its account and turned it into a standing rule.

claims.claim: ARCS's decision scoring is accurate.
claims.evidence: Each decision is scored when made and closed against its outcome. Not enough outcomes have closed to publish an accuracy figure, so none is claimed.
